findings.issue: 米 standalone meaning 'rice' is read こめ, never べい (on-reading used only in compounds like 米国). The kana teaches a wrong reading for the whole sentence.
findings.current: べいわあたたかいくにでできる。
findings.suggested: こめわあたたかいくにでできる。

findings.issue: Same wrong reading propagated to romaji: 米 = kome here, not bei.
Token 米 ('rice', the sentence topic) has reading べい; in this context (standalone noun 'rice') the reading is こめ.
講義をする means to GIVE/deliver a lecture; 'to take a class' reverses the participant role (attending vs teaching) and contradicts en ('I will lecture on literature') and expl_en ('to give a lecture').
findings.current: To take a class on literature.
findings.suggested: To give a lecture on literature.

findings.issue: 壁 means 'wall', not 'fence' (fence would be 塀/柵). The en contradicts lit_en ('The wall...'), the token gloss 'wall', and pt ('o muro'); the Tatoeba paired English was adopted unchanged but is unfaithful to the Japanese.
findings.current: The fence fell with a great crash.
findings.suggested: The wall fell with a great crash.

findings.issue: 聞きたい expresses desire — exactly the 〜たい point the explanation teaches; 'need' misstates it as necessity and clashes with lit_en ('...who wants to hear it') and pt ('Eu quero ouvir isso').

Internal course metadata leaked into the learner-facing explanation: a note about a 'stated target かな' that does not occur in the sentence. Confusing for beginners and irrelevant to the 〜ないでくれ structure being explained; it also reveals a wrong grammar-target link.
findings.current: The stated target is かな ('I wonder if...?'), but it does NOT appear here: the sentence ends in くれ, an informal request, not in a question with かな.
findings.suggested: (delete this sentence — internal target-mismatch note, not learner-facing content)

findings.issue: Same internal target-mismatch note leaked into the pt explanation ('O alvo declarado é かな...'); it is not learner-facing content and confuses the actual 〜ないでくれ lesson.
findings.current: O alvo declarado é かな ('será que...?'), mas ele NÃO aparece aqui: a frase termina em くれ, um pedido informal, não numa pergunta com かな.
findings.suggested: (remover esta frase — nota interna de divergência de alvo, não é conteúdo didático)

findings.issue: ふんいき requires the syllabic-n apostrophe: fun'iki. 'funiki' collapses ん+い and reads as ふにき. This is a real reading ambiguity, not the known punctuation/katakana romaji issue.
